tagline: Structured prompts tuned for GPT's conversational, general-purpose strengths.
whenToUse: Use ChatGPT-optimized prompts for everyday writing, brainstorming, research summaries, coding help, and general Q&A where you want a fast, well-rounded response without heavy customization.

strengths.title: General-purpose reasoning
strengths.description: Strong all-round reasoning and broad knowledge coverage across most everyday tasks.

strengths.title: Conversational refinement
strengths.description: Handles multi-turn conversation and follow-up refinement well, so you can iterate in the same thread.

strengths.title: Format following
strengths.description: Good at following explicit formatting instructions — tables, lists, JSON, and other strict output shapes.

strengths.title: Ecosystem
strengths.description: Wide plugin and tool ecosystem for extended tasks like browsing, code execution, and file analysis.

badPrompt: Write me a blog post about productivity.
goodPrompt:
Role: You are a productivity coach writing for busy freelancers.
Action: Write a 700-word blog post titled "Why Time Blocking Fails Most People."
Context: Open with a relatable scenario. Include three specific mistakes with fixes.
Layout/Length: End with one actionable takeaway. Tone: conversational, no jargon.
exampleOutput: A 700-word post with a clear angle and a real hook, rather than a generic listicle — three concrete mistakes, each paired with a fix, and a single closing takeaway readers can act on today.

tagline: Structured prompts tuned for Claude's careful reasoning and long-context strengths.
whenToUse: Use Claude-optimized prompts for long-document analysis, nuanced writing, careful multi-step reasoning, coding with large context, and tasks where tone and constraints genuinely matter.

strengths.title: Long-context handling
strengths.description: Strong at working across large documents or codebases without losing track of earlier details.

strengths.title: Careful writing
strengths.description: Nuanced writing with good instruction-following on tone, constraints, and audience.

strengths.title: Structured reasoning
strengths.description: Reasons well step by step when a prompt asks it to show its work.

strengths.title: Handles ambiguity
strengths.description: Will ask clarifying questions when prompted to, rather than guessing silently.

goodPrompt:
Role: You are a research analyst.
Action: Read the attached report and produce a 5-bullet executive summary.
Context: Audience is a non-technical VP. Prioritize business impact over methodology.
Example: Flag any claims that lack supporting data, similar to how an analyst would annotate a memo before forwarding it.
exampleOutput: A 5-bullet summary a VP could act on without a follow-up question — business impact first, methodology skipped unless it changes the conclusion, and any unsupported claims clearly flagged.

tagline: Structured prompts tuned for Gemini's multimodal and research strengths.
whenToUse: Use Gemini-optimized prompts for multimodal tasks (text plus image or video context), research that benefits from current information, and workflows tied into the Google ecosystem.

strengths.title: Multimodal understanding
strengths.description: Strong at reasoning across text, image, and video context in the same prompt.

strengths.title: Grounded research
strengths.description: Good integration with search grounding for tasks that need current information.

strengths.title: Structured extraction
strengths.description: Solid at structured data extraction and side-by-side comparison tasks.

strengths.title: Long context
strengths.description: Competitive long-context handling for large inputs.

goodPrompt:
Role: You are a shopping assistant for a budget-conscious first-time buyer.
Action: Compare Product A and Product B.
Layout/Length: Output a table with columns: Feature, Product A, Product B, Winner. Follow with a 2-sentence recommendation.
exampleOutput: A clean comparison table by feature, followed by a short, decisive recommendation — not a meandering paragraph comparison.

tagline: Structured prompts covering subject, style, lighting, and composition for image generators.
whenToUse: Use image-optimized prompts for concept art, product mockups, cinematic stills, portraits, and any visual generation task where a vague prompt produces inconsistent results.

strengths.title: Style control
strengths.description: Precise control over style and mood when a prompt specifies it explicitly rather than leaving it implied.

strengths.title: Composition & lighting
strengths.description: Naming composition and lighting language yields far more consistent results across generations.

strengths.title: Reference modifiers
strengths.description: Film stock, lens, and artist-style modifiers meaningfully shift the output when named directly.

strengths.title: Cross-model portability
strengths.description: Works across most major image generators with only minor syntax adjustments.

goodPrompt:
Subject: A weathered industrial robot standing in a rain-soaked alley at night.
Context: Neon signage reflected in puddles.
Layout/Style: Cinematic lighting, shallow depth of field, shot on 35mm film, moody blue-orange color grade.
exampleOutput: A far more art-directed image than a one-line description would produce — consistent mood, lighting, and framing because the prompt named them instead of leaving them to chance.
